SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has consistently run ahead of system credit growth — advances +15.2% YoY in Jun'22 vs system 3.28% YTD, +15.82% in Jun'24, +18.64% in Jun'26 — and it was not bought with credit quality (slippage ratio 1.36% to 0.83%, PCR 93.8%); but no explicit market-share numbers versus named competitors are ever given, and the deposit side is losing ground (CD ratio stretched to 82-83%).
SHAREGAIN.quote: Global Gross Advances increased by 18.64% YoY... in the domestic arena, we have done a growth of about 9% year-on-year, vis-à-vis industry and banking system's growth of 3.28%

CULTURE.rationale: Over four years the team largely delivered what it promised — GNPA from 9.30% (Jun'22) to 1.81% (Jun'26), net NPA below 1% by FY25 as targeted, the 2022 digital roadmap shipped, ECLGS 5.0 sanctions of Rs.6,000 crore against an Rs.8,000 crore guide, and ECL transition prepared ahead of the 2027 deadline with CRAR at 18.69% — with stable leadership (Karnatak MD since FY23, Rajagopal ED throughout); but bad news is surfaced only when analysts ask, and NIM/CASA slippage is not owned as a miss.
CULTURE.quote: we have already done a lot of homework and preparation since the draft guidelines have come... the impact will be only 0.50 % p.a

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing described would stop a rival: the same products (gold loans, co-lending, FCNR mobilisation, digital platforms) are being launched by every PSU and private bank, borrowers switch on rate, and the bank itself flags peers undercutting it on price while it stretches its CD ratio to 82-83% to fund growth.
MOATTEST.quote: it's a product all even public sector banks have started offering

RECURRING.rationale: Across all excerpted calls (Aug 2022 to Jun 2026) there is no discussion of subscriptions, AMC/service revenue, renewal or attach rates, or customer advances funding the business; the model is outright product sale to retail and to franchise partners.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No prescriber/installer/professional intermediary is described anywhere; sales are direct-to-consumer through own stores, franchise, MBOs and e-commerce. Franchisee and MBO engagement programmes are trade distribution, not an expert recommender who chooses on the customer's behalf.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Bata sells finished consumer footwear; there is no evidence in any call of a critical-but-tiny-share input, certification/standards anchoring, or customers who cannot switch.

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a persistent and itemised cost/efficiency culture across the four years — flexi manpower and variabilised store pay (Aug 2022, Aug 2024), plant closure and structural employee-cost reduction, 30% complexity reduction and inventory down 28% over two years (Jun 2026) — plus a mass-end 'value proposition' push; but the low-price-plus economics never appear, with turns still at ~2.7 versus a target of 3 and stagnant volumes rather than scale-driven turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: our employee cost is lower by about 10%. And this benefit is flowing from -- to the employee cost line item on a structural basis

PRICING.rationale: The record shows the opposite of pricing power: routine EOSS and high-single-digit average discounting (Aug 2024), gross margins repeatedly flat or optically diluted, mass price points under stress for '7, 8 quarters', and by Jun 2026 management is cautious rather than confident about passing 5-6% raw-material inflation. Premium growth (Hush Puppies, Power) is mix shift, not price realisation.
PRICING.quote: we have obviously taken in the judicious price elasticity that we need to apply

BRAND.rationale: Heritage and reach are real and repeatedly evidenced — highest-ever brand consideration of 66, high and climbing unaided awareness, sustained A&P at 250-300bps with two consecutive quarters of double-digit marketing growth (Feb/Jun 2026), and stretch into Floatz, Power Apparel and Nine West. But the brand does not convert into the pattern's proof points: no share gain and no premium pricing, and management is directly challenged on Bata being seen as a legacy brand by younger consumers with the answer still 'in works'.
BRAND.quote: The brand is extremely high on awareness, and it continues to climb

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur each year with revenue traction — Sneaker Studios (125 in 2022 to 740 by 2024), Floatz at ~4.5% of retail, Power technology launches, Nine West, and the reimagined product funnel plus zero-based merchandising scaled 400 to 550 stores by Jun 2026. But no R&D spend is ever disclosed, innovation has not yet lifted growth or gross margin, and management concedes most of the product investment is not yet visible.
INNOVATION.quote: There is a huge amount of investment that are going in. I think only 10% of that is what has come out into what is consumer facing

FORWARD.rationale: This is the clearest and most consistently delivered pattern: the Aug 2022 franchise vision was pursued every quarter to ~2,000 EBOs and 700+ franchise stores by Jun 2026, with half of new franchise additions from existing partners, franchisees funding inventory under an outright model (better ROCE), plus SIS panels, 1,670-town MBO reach, own Power/Floatz banners and kiosks, a D2C app already at 14% of D2C, and 700+ omni-fulfilling stores.
FORWARD.quote: an ROCE by default franchise is much better because a lot of the inventory and working capital is loaded onto the franchise because we follow an outright model

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Over the four years covered, revenue went from negative same-store sales (Aug 2024) to only ~3-5% growth by FY26, with no share statistics ever cited and competition from Metro and global brands increasing; management itself accepts the four-year stagnation premise and offers no share-gain counter-evidence.
SHAREGAIN.quote: over the last 4 years, revenue growth has remained largely stagnant despite multiple strategic initiatives

CULTURE.rationale: Bad news is disclosed plainly and accounting is conservative — the disappointing quarter owned in Aug 2024, full charge-off of ERP costs, exceptional items itemised in Jun 2026 — and Gunjan Shah has led continuously since FY2022 delivering the franchise, inventory and ZBM promises made in earlier calls. Against that, the headline double-digit growth aspiration has gone undelivered for years, the finance seat turned over three times (Vidhya Srinivasan, Anil Somani, Amit Aggarwal) and the board list churned heavily.
CULTURE.quote: And therefore, I think a longer term trend line, obviously disappointing revenue growth last quarter

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-rebuild assets are evidenced — a ~95-year brand with top-of-mind awareness, 2,000+ EBOs, ~20,000 MBO outlets across 1,670 towns, and franchisee relationships deep enough that half of new stores come from existing partners. But management concedes the category is fragmented at both ends with new entrants (Metro acquiring brand rights, global digital brands) contesting it, and the advantage is not visibly stopping them.
MOATTEST.quote: both ends, the market is significantly fragmented

RECURRING.rationale: Across all three meets the revenue model is described purely as seasonal, weather-dependent product sell-through (liquidation of crop protection and corn seed) with no licences, AMCs, subscriptions, renewal or attach rates; cash discussion is about collections and receivables, not customer advances or deferred revenue funding the business.
RECURRING.quote: we were extremely vigilant and careful that we do not want to leave a lot of inventory in the market, and also risk collections

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through a retail/dealer channel plus 1,500+ Better Life Farming centres and agri-entrepreneurs who advise farmers, and by Nov 2025 management is deliberately handing whole geographies to partners who 'service the farmer' — but the farmer is also the payer and Bayer spends heavily on direct farmer brand-building and digital outreach, so the classic prescriber-pays-nothing dynamic is only half present.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: these partners, equipped with a broader portfolio, are better partners to the farmer than I am

TOLLROAD.rationale: Rather than customers paying without negotiating, management repeatedly calls India 'a very competitive market' and in FY25 could not pass through input cost inflation because of Chinese supply and pricing — EPS fell from 165 to 126; there is no certification, standards or 'don't switch once converted' language.
TOLLROAD.quote: the supply and the prices from China were such, that it limited our ability to pass any price increase in the market

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is genuine cost discipline (OpEx CAGR 6.1% vs 9% sales, flat quarterly OpEx despite inflation), but the strategy is the opposite of low-price-plus-scale: in Nov 2025 they prioritise the profitable portfolio, withdraw manpower from low-margin territories and measure margin per head rather than chasing volume.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our turnover per head doesn't help me when that turnover is not profitable and the head is expensive

PRICING.rationale: Pricing power is real but conditional: FY23 held Roundup top line on price, corn seeds grew on both volume and price through FY25, yet FY25 was a 'perfect storm' where Chinese generic pricing blocked any pass-through and margins/EPS fell sharply — management itself frames pricing as something the portfolio 'has enabled over the years' but not last year.
PRICING.quote: On one hand, we were not able to increase our prices; something which our portfolio has enabled over the years

BRAND.rationale: Repeatedly anchored on heritage and consistency — 125+ years in India, 50 years of Roundup, 25 years of Dekalb — with sustained brand-building spend, a named top-brand stable (Dekalb, Roundup, Nativo, Laudis, Council Activ) that 'continued to progress well' through bad weather, and an anti-counterfeit scan feature in FarmRise precisely because the brand is worth faking.
BRAND.quote: 25 years of Dekalb, you might have seen it before, 50 years of roundup

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur across the whole period with stated revenue/margin impact — Vayego, Laudis and Council in 2023, fast hybrid turnover 9108 to 9208, Bicota and Etcio Star in 2025 — and the Nov 2025 turnaround plan explicitly rests on 'backing on our R&D pipeline' with launches chosen for profitability profile, though India-level R&D spend is never disclosed since the pipeline is the parent's.
INNOVATION.quote: you will be hearing of Bicota in the market... I'm sitting here and it's actually having impact on my bottom line

FORWARD.rationale: Clear movement toward the farmer — 1,500+ Better Life Farming retail centres, e-commerce, FarmRise direct digital connect, and in 2024 'Bayer literally starting to own the retail' — but by Nov 2025 the model pivots to third-party partner-run retail for OPEX reasons, and no own-store count, royalty stream or D2C revenue share is ever quantified.
FORWARD.quote: this is starting to be a new go to market for me where buyer literally starting to own the retail

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is evident in corn — the portfolio doubled over five years at 15-16% CAGR on volume and price, they claim to be the main corn breeder in India and are 'really taking market share' in new states like Karnataka — but core Crop Protection grew under 6% CAGR and they are deliberately ceding low-margin territories to partners, so gains are selective, not persistent across the business.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we've gone into areas where, in the past we were very, very timid; Karnataka etc. where we're really, really taking market share

CULTURE.rationale: Bad news is disclosed promptly and unspun across all three meets ('you saw a very honest 23-24', the FY25 margin collapse laid out, receivables errors admitted), the liquidation-over-sell-in discipline promised in 2023 was still being enforced in 2025 at the cost of reported sales, and capital discipline is consistent — ROCE up 500bps over four years, ~80-90% of operating cash returned as dividend, dividend held at Rs.90 through the down year.
CULTURE.quote: we did have some issues with receivables, and yes, we've learned our lesson

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — decades of corn germplasm and breeding leadership, global registrations and R&D, 125-year presence and reach to ~20 million smallholders — but the FY25 experience shows the crop protection base is exposed to Chinese generic supply, and management's answer is portfolio pruning and backward integration rather than an articulated barrier a funded entrant could not cross.
MOATTEST.quote: we are the main breeders in the country, there's no question about it

RECURRING.rationale: Managed services, warranty/tech support and AMC-type wins appear in deal disclosures (Q1 FY25: managed/on-demand deals >$13mn) and management talks of converting lumpy projects into annuity, but across all 16 calls there are no attach rates, renewal rates or deferred-revenue-as-funding disclosures — and working capital is a cash drain, with debt drawn to fund it (Q1 FY23).
RECURRING.quote: a project business is not a quarter-on-quarter business, but we are turning it into an annuity mode business with our pipeline

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The 20%-of-revenue Technology Product Solutions arm goes to market entirely through two-tier distribution, VARs and integration partners, with Black Box funding technical enablement and quality support for those partners; but the GSI business (80%) sells direct to enterprises, and no professional-training/certification lock-in of the channel is described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: the go-to-market is through integration partners... we provide hi-tech engagement for customers to evangelize their product and provide technical and quality support to our partners

TOLLROAD.rationale: Black Box sells large, discretionary capex-linked infrastructure projects, not a tiny critical input — revenue repeatedly slipped because customers deferred decisions on Fed rates and budget cycles (Q1 FY25) and management had to exit thousands of accounts and cut guidance (Q3 FY26), the opposite of un-negotiated toll collection.
TOLLROAD.quote: the customers are also prudently going on with respect to spending, because if they go slow on the work, obviously, their spending a little bit gets slowed

LOWPRICE.rationale: A genuine and itemised cost culture runs through the whole record — $10–15mn overlay cost removal (Aug 2022), procurement centralisation, India GCC offshoring worth 100–200bps, 22 ERPs consolidated to one stack, subcontractors insourced, 470bps EBITDA expansion FY23–FY26 — but this is restructuring toward normal margins, not a low-price-plus-scale competitive weapon; they raised prices and walked away from price-sensitive volume.
LOWPRICE.quote: We reduced SG&A costs, consolidated facilities, transitioned subcontractor labour to our own workforce and simplified our customer portfolio by exiting thousands of low-value accounts

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly reprices contracts for labour/input inflation and lifted prices on low-value accounts, and cites 'pricing discipline' in Q3 FY26 — but the volume cost was real (revenue fell 9% YoY in Q1 FY25 from those exits) and gross margin compressed to ~27.7% under inflation in FY23, so this is cost pass-through rather than durable pricing power.
PRICING.quote: we have been gradually increasing prices to our low end customers or exiting if we don't see value

BRAND.rationale: The Black Box name carries 50 years of heritage, 120+ Fortune 500 customers and decades-long mission-critical relationships that management calls its most durable advantage — but there is no A&P spend, no premium pricing evidence, and the product arm is explicitly white-label branded, so brand shows as trust/credentialing rather than pricing or share power.
BRAND.quote: These are long-standing partnerships, some of them over decades, that have believed in Black Box to provide mission-critical environments where execution, reliability, and trust are non-negotiable

INNOVATION.rationale: Two R&D centres (Ireland, Bangalore) support market-leading KVM/AV products and INR410cr of the FY25 raise was earmarked partly for innovation in cloud/cyber/AI/IoT, but R&D spend is never quantified or tracked across calls, and the core 80% GSI business integrates other vendors' technology under 'best-of-breed' partnerships rather than proprietary innovation.
INNOVATION.quote: We have two R&D centers in Ireland and in Bangalore. Our products are market leader in space.

FORWARD.rationale: Black Box moves the other way — its own products reach end customers via ScanSource/TD Synnex/Ingram two-tier distribution and integration partners, and there is no own-store, franchise, royalty or D2C economics anywhere in the 16 calls.
FORWARD.quote: our product business it's sold through two tier distribution like any IP-based product manufacturers

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Backlog compounding from ~$475mn (Jun 2024) to >$800mn (Mar 2026, +60% YoY) on ~$1bn FY26 bookings, four of the top six hyperscalers and four of the top five US banks, plus Brazil entry via 2S, evidence real wallet-share capture — but no explicit market-share numbers versus named competitors, and headline revenue actually shrank in FY25 while guidance was cut in FY26.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the order backlog is now expected to exceed our earlier estimate and reach around $800 million by the end of March 2026... reflecting a growth of 60% year-on-year

CULTURE.rationale: Stable leadership (Verma MD since FY2021 with the same CFO across all 16 calls), promoter Essar putting in ~INR425cr of fresh capital, D/E cut 1.2→0.6, explicit ROCE framing (34% cumulative) and the delivered 9% EBITDA margin promised back in Aug 2022 all point to long-term-minded execution; against that, the Rs 7,000cr-by-FY24 revenue promise was missed by years and FY26 guidance was cut mid-year, and investors have called out the pattern on the calls.
CULTURE.quote: We're constantly missing on our top line and our commentary hasn't changed.

MOATTEST.rationale: The advantages cited — global delivery footprint, partner certifications, customer relationships — are exactly what Black Box itself bought rather than built (Black Box Corp in 2019, 2S in Brazil in 2026), and a well-funded integrator can acquire the same; the ~9% EBITDA margin and dependence on third-party fiber, racks and OEM technology confirm no un-replicable barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: The acquisition of 2S in Brazil that we announced recently is in the direction of creating scale in markets that are sub-scale today for us.

RECURRING.rationale: Neither AGM discusses attach rates, AMC/service revenue, renewals, installed base or customer advances; the businesses described (tea, coffee, auto components, dental consumables) are one-off product sales.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The healthcare division sells dental products whose demand is gated by dentists and dental colleges rather than end-patients, but across both calls management offers no discussion of training programmes, prescriber loyalty or channel investment — only demand recovery post-COVID.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Primarily due to opening of the dental colleges and clinics post COVID, better product mix and realization of higher prices for alloys

TOLLROAD.rationale: No discussion in either AGM of the product being a trivial share of customer cost, certification/standards anchoring, or customers not switching once converted.

LOWPRICE.rationale: No cost culture or itemised savings anywhere; on the contrary a shareholder noted tea realisations running below South Indian cost of production, and management cited scale economics as the reason for exiting coffee entirely.
LOWPRICE.quote: The coffee business, although profitable has given very low yield and returns over the years due to its very nature of business. By agriculture and economy of scale

PRICING.rationale: Prices move with commodity and input markets, not with pricing power: FY22 tea sold at a lower average price, FY23 tea got Rs5/kg more but volumes fell 4.19 lakh kg, coffee realisation swung Rs186 to Rs280, and dental price rises were alloy pass-through.
PRICING.quote: Revenue of tea decreased by 4 crores due to the decrease in sales quantity by 4.19 lakhs despite higher average price of INR5 a kilo

BRAND.rationale: 157/158 years of heritage and the Wadia/Britannia association are repeatedly invoked, but that brand equity sits in the listed investee, not in BBTC's own tea, auto-component or dental operations, and no A&P spend, premium pricing or adjacency launch is discussed.
BRAND.quote: We are a good holding company for Britannia, which we get returns

INNOVATION.rationale: The Electro Mags components division quantified revenue from newly released products in FY22 and grew 133 to 151.7 crores in FY23, but no R&D spend, pipeline or share-of-industry-R&D is ever disclosed, and management frames the growth as riding industry demand rather than leading it.
INNOVATION.quote: The division developed and released new products with 2302 lakhs in the year 21-22

FORWARD.rationale: No mention of own stores, franchising, licensing, D2C or distribution ownership in either AGM.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: No share figures are given in either year; management cites rising industry-wide forecasts while noting new entrants crowding in, and the corporation divested coffee and shrank plantation volumes rather than gaining ground.
SHAREGAIN.quote: several Indian and international players have entered the industry

CULTURE.rationale: The 2023 call carried a qualified audit opinion and a Rs1,865 crore Go Airlines impairment that flipped consolidated profit of 808 crores into a 533-crore loss, blame was placed entirely on Pratt & Whitney with no reflection on the capital-allocation decision, and shareholder questions in both years were deflected to written replies — one investor's balance-sheet error flagged three years running.
CULTURE.quote: But sir, from last three years, I'm asking you one thing about the wrong printing in the balance sheet

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in either call articulates why a funded newcomer could not replicate these businesses; the coffee estates were sold to pay down debt precisely because returns lagged the land value, and the auto-components division openly faces new entrants.
MOATTEST.quote: The corporation has divested the coffee business for 291 crores to reduce the overall debt

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls the company discusses only outright product sales of biscuits and bakery items; no licence fees, AMC/service contracts, subscriptions, attach rates, renewal rates or deferred revenue as a funding source are ever mentioned.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is created by consumer-facing marketing and trade promotions, not by an expert prescriber — management explicitly reallocated budget to consumer promotions to defend share, and runs consumer campaigns (Slice of Trust, Maa Se Happiness, Blinkit collaborations); the B2B QSR customers are price-negotiating buyers, not recommenders.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we also had to join to ensure that we are able to kind of retain our market share

TOLLROAD.rationale: Biscuits and bread are the customer's own product, not a tiny critical input; the calls describe intense price and promotion competition, coinage-price battles (INR4.50 vs INR5) and full pass-through of GST benefits — the opposite of a non-negotiated toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: the competition intensity has increased quite significantly, especially on account of the market leaders taking an aggressive stance on consumer promotions

LOWPRICE.rationale: Project IMPACT (from FY24 onward) is a genuine, repeatedly referenced institutionalised cost programme and the company competes at INR5/INR10 price points passing GST savings fully to consumers, but there is no itemised cost-leadership disclosure and it is a scale follower to Parle/Britannia rather than the low-cost benchmark.
LOWPRICE.quote: Structured mindset of cost optimization was institutionalised through project impact

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly takes price/grammage actions to recover input inflation (FY23 hikes, FY26 3% inflation recovery) and pushes premiumisation, but this is cost pass-through rather than pricing above inflation — and the FY26 coinage episode shows price is set by the market leader, with volume/share consequences.
PRICING.quote: we had moved to INR5 and Britannia moved to INR5 and so that definitely had its impact

BRAND.rationale: English Oven shows real brand pull (high-teens growth for four straight years, brand-led entry into Kolkata/Hyderabad) and the name is stretched into adjacencies (Zero Maida, NaturBaked protein bread, frozen desserts, Cheesecake Jars), and Cremica carries 50+ export markets — but the core domestic biscuit brand commands no pricing premium and grew only 6.7% in FY26.
BRAND.quote: English Oven's strong trajectory is underpinned by brand pull, health -first initiatives and distribution excellence

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new products appear every year with commercial traction (Non-Stop cracker, Zero Maida, Golden Bites, NaturBaked protein bread, frozen/ready-to-eat range now ~20% of B2B bakery) and gross margin reached 48%, but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and innovation is recipe/format-level rather than a technology moat.
INNOVATION.quote: our innovative frozen bakery products, as I had mentioned in our last call, also continues to grow

FORWARD.rationale: There are no own stores or franchising, but the company deliberately builds direct digital channels — q-commerce declared a 'channel of significance', e-commerce-first launches, Blinkit tie-ups reaching 3 lakh households — plus SFA/DMS and handheld billing to control the route to market.
FORWARD.quote: we have been and will be deliberately building quick commerce as a channel of significance

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Revenue compounded 20% over FY22–FY26 (INR988cr to INR2,044cr) with genuine geographic expansion (Indore, Kolkata, Khopoli, Hyderabad, 70+ export countries), but in domestic biscuits management describes retaining rather than gaining share, and FY26 biscuit growth of 6.7% was below its own aspiration.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have been able to very well retain our market shares over the last two quarters

CULTURE.rationale: Promoter family with long-tenured leadership, conservative balance sheet (0.36x debt/equity, QIP taken to avoid leverage), deliberate professionalisation, delivered the stated INR2,000cr revenue goal and the promised Rajpura/Indore/Kolkata/Khopoli plants, and openly owns errors — but the 13–14% EBITDA aspiration stated in Aug 2022 was still unmet at 12.6% in FY26 and Khopoli slipped from FY25 to FY26.
CULTURE.quote: probably this time was a miss because one of a very large player decided to stay at a lower pricing

MOATTEST.rationale: The assets described — greenfield biscuit and bread lines, distribution feet-on-street, SFA/DMS — are all buyable by a funded entrant within a few years, and the calls show the company forced to follow market-leader pricing and promotions, which is the signature of a replicable position rather than a durable barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: domestic biscuit business has been for a while a very highly competitive and intense business

RECURRING.rationale: BEL wins the platform then earns AMC, spares and maintenance annuities off the installed base (Akash AMC, P15B communication spares, maintaining the AEW&CS aircraft, repeat squadrons/states for Akash and LRSAM), and the business is funded by customer advances — INR12,500 crores at FY26 year-end against ~INR27,480 crores revenue. But services are only ~11% of mix and management never quantifies attach or renewal rates.
RECURRING.quote: Advances as of the year end is around INR12,500 crores from the customers.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: BEL is frequently specified into platforms by intermediaries — DRDO nominates it as development-cum-production partner, and shipyards/HAL integrate it as 'buyer nominated equipment' while MoD pays — but the calls show no professional-training or channel-relationship machinery, and the Netra 2 loss shows the intermediary can switch.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: there are umpteen buyer nominated equipments in these

TOLLROAD.rationale: The evidence contradicts the 'tiny share of customer cost' test: management says electronics is 25-30% of a submarine's value and BEL's content sits at the centre of programme cost, and pricing is set by L1 tendering rather than certification or standards anchoring.
TOLLROAD.quote: around 25% to 30% typically comes to electronics portion generally

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is real, itemised cost discipline — material consumption cut from 64.95% to 61.95% in Q1 FY23 with a stated 200bps target, and indigenisation used to offset imported semiconductor inflation — but this is a high-margin (28-30% EBITDA), moderate-turns business, not the low-margin/high-asset-turn scale model, and it lost Netra 2 on price.
LOWPRICE.quote: our material consumption in the Q1 has come down to 61.95% from 64.95%

PRICING.rationale: Across all 17 calls there is not one discussion of raising prices; gross margin is guided flat at 40-42%, input cost increases are absorbed and offset by indigenisation rather than passed on, and contracts are won by L1 competitive bidding — which BEL lost on Netra 2. Margin expansion came from cost and mix, not price.
PRICING.quote: we are in the process of indigenizing some of the technology itself. And that way, we will compensate for this price offset

BRAND.rationale: BEL carries genuine institutional standing — a 1954-vintage MoD enterprise treated as the default partner for complex programmes ('de facto leader', 50-60% of submarine electronics) — but there is no A&P spend, no premium pricing, no distributor leverage and no consumer-style adjacency stretch.
BRAND.quote: this large complex domain solution, right now we are the de facto leader

INNOVATION.rationale: Sustained, disclosed, self-funded innovation: ~82% of turnover from indigenous technology with ~40% BEL's own designs and a stated target to raise that to 75%; Central Research Labs and PDICs; named new systems every year (ALNS Mk-II with NavIC, Uttam-class radar modules, D2-D4 counter-drone, quantum-safe comms) and INR100-200 crores of AI/HPC compute capex in FY26 — with management arguing new technology lifts margins.
INNOVATION.quote: 82% of the turnover is coming from indigenous technology... remaining 40 is from BEL's own developed product and systems

SHAREGAIN.rationale: BEL holds commanding content share on new platforms (50-60% of P-75I electronics, ~30/30/30 across Army/Navy/Air Force) and exports are scaling from a low base (TRDS TR modules, Airbus C295, Guatemala solar), but no rising share numbers are ever quantified and the FY27 call concedes ground to private entrants — losing the Netra 2 system-integration role to Adani.
SHAREGAIN.quote: more than 50% to 60% of electronics in this program will be from BEL

CULTURE.rationale: Guidance made and met repeatedly over four years — 15% revenue growth promised in Jul 2022 and delivered, 16% in FY26 with 'all the guidance parameters' met — alongside prompt disclosure of bad news (chip-shortage revenue slippage quantified at INR2,600 crores, LD and doubtful-debt provisions rising to INR132 crores, losing the Netra 2 bid), a net-cash balance sheet and rising receivable discipline (176 to 140 days). The caveat is PSU leadership churn: four chairmen across FY21-FY25.
CULTURE.quote: we have met all the guidance parameters in the last financial year

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real, articulable barriers — seven decades of platform-specific know-how across 29 SBUs, DRDO's designation of BEL as lead production partner on the most complex programmes, security-cleared facilities and a maintained installed base — but the same calls show a well-funded newcomer closing the gap, with Adani taking the Netra 2 system-integration role on price.
MOATTEST.quote: we also participated in the bid, but unfortunately, we were not L1

RECURRING.rationale: Across all seven calls there is no mention of service/AMC contracts, licences, subscriptions, attach or renewal rates, or customer advances/deferred revenue as a funding source; revenue is purely OEM component sales at programme prices.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: There is no intermediating professional — the OEM both specifies and pays, and Belrise wins on nomination, quality-cost-delivery and technology shows for OEM engineering teams, not via a trade channel it trains.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we hosted a technology show for one of India's largest and most established four-wheeler OEMs at the premises

TOLLROAD.rationale: Single-source nomination on mission-critical parts and the aerospace assets show toll-road traits (Chester Hall's sub-micron aero-engine parts, 'only one other supplier in the country' for the 650cc premium component), but the core 2W chassis is ~INR12,500-20,300 of content per vehicle — a material, negotiated share of OEM cost with back-to-back RM pricing, not a <1-2% unnegotiated toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: only one other supplier in the country capable of producing such components at comparable standards

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a consistent cost/asset-turn orientation — warehouses near customers to avoid sub-scale plants, filling spare ACED capacity for operating leverage, Haridwar built off existing plants to limit greenfield capex, and India as a 'best cost' aerospace hub — but no itemised cost culture and margins are ordinary auto-supplier (12-13%), so scale-driven low-price-plus is only partially evidenced.
LOWPRICE.quote: The plant will receive components from multiple existing facilities... while limiting incremental greenfield capex

PRICING.rationale: Management explicitly describes a pass-through model rather than pricing power: raw material moves are passed to customers with a lag, EBITDA margins are flat-to-down (12.5% H1 FY26 to 11.4% in Q4 FY26), and growth comes from content per vehicle and new programmes, never from price increases.
PRICING.quote: our business operates on a back-to-back pricing model for raw materials... effectively passed through to our customers, with a certain lag

BRAND.rationale: A B2B nominated supplier with no consumer brand, no A&P spend, no distribution leverage and no adjacency launches under a brand name; the company was in fact renamed from Badve Engineering to Belrise in 2025, and wins are attributed to engineering and QCD performance.
BRAND.quote: our consistent quality, cost, and delivery parameters for that program has translated into this expanded business award

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a real, repeated innovation record — 160-member product development team, 800+ robots, patented suspensions, steering columns, cross-car beams, 1000 MPa high-tensile via H-One, copper bus bars via the merger — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and gross margins are not high enough to fund outsized R&D, so it is capability-led rather than R&D-dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: we have recently started making and supplying suspension systems, which we hold a patent for, and steering columns, which was a monopoly product historically

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C anywhere in the record; the 'forward' movement described is toward the OEM (Tier 1 to Tier 0.5 system assembly) plus backward verticalisation via the Badve Autocomps/Eximius merger — the opposite direction from the pattern.
FORWARD.quote: moving from being a component supplier to co-creator and full-system supplier - into a concept we call Tier-0.5 supplier

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is quantified and repeated across the year: 24% of Indian 2W metal components, plastics share going 10% to ~25% post-merger with >30% wallet-share uplift at a marquee OEM, content per vehicle 12,500 to 17,300 to 20,300, 4W +37% and CV +35% in FY26, plus taking over a distressed Tier 1's business at a Japanese OEM — and it is won on delivery, not price or credit.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Post-merger, the combined entity will command nearly a 25% market share in 2-wheeler plastic components

CULTURE.rationale: Founder-led family business (promoters ~66.5%, MD plus two sons) that opened its FY26 call by scoring itself against each IPO-year promise and delivered them, discloses bad news promptly (GST-related September slowdown, customer cyberattack, INR94.7 million one-time aerospace loss, Q4 wage and logistics cost pressure), cut net debt from INR9,614 million to INR5,977 million and manages to ROCE; the large promoter-entity related-party book (INR11.5 billion) is a legacy governance flag, but it was resolved by merging those entities in at ~book value, an 8.3x P/E versus Belrise's 30.9x.
CULTURE.quote: Our first commitment was to deliver mid-teens revenue growth while keeping our EBITDA margins stable. And I am glad to share that we achieved this.

MOATTEST.rationale: Some barriers are concretely un-replicable — JIPM TPM awards with a 5-7 year gestation, sub-micron aero-engine machining where 'only a handful of suppliers in the world' qualify, single-source nomination on 200-250 component subsystems, 1000 MPa high-tensile capability — but the core 2W sheet-metal pressing base is capital-and-time replicable, and Belrise itself bought entry into filtration, high-tensile and aerospace cheaply (INR165 million, INR1,900 million, EUR 0.35 million), which shows these capabilities can be acquired.
MOATTEST.quote: parts that are mission-critical and that only a handful of suppliers in the world are capable of producing

RECURRING.rationale: A large installed base (9,000+ HMVs, 33,100 M&C machines, 18,000 rail coaches, 1,400 units in 73 countries) does generate overhaul/AMC and spares revenue that management calls high-margin, and a hub-and-spoke spares warehouse is being rolled out — but across all six calls there are no attach rates, renewal rates, or customer advances described as a funding source, and collections/working capital are repeatedly a problem rather than a source of float.
RECURRING.quote: we have also around 20% of service revenue... spares and service businesses, which has a poten■ally high margin, high growth

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The calls are silent on any professional intermediary; sales go directly to Coal India, MoD, metro corporations and MDOs through tenders, with no discussion of trade training or channel influence.

TOLLROAD.rationale: BEML sells large capital equipment that is a major line item for the buyer, not a sub-1% critical input — management explicitly describes customers deferring capex, switching to opex models and buying second-hand instead, the opposite of 'don't switch once converted'.
TOLLROAD.quote: the MDOs prefer not to invest in CapEx but in OpEx. And, rather than high-end mining equipment, they will go for lower-end mining equipment where we are not present... they would also sometimes prefer the second-hand equipment

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is fixed-cost discipline talk (manpower as % of sales, checkpoints on fixed cost), but management concedes its own cost base is above industry norm and pricing on nomination orders is cost-plus set by the customer at 2.5–7.5% — low margins without the offsetting cost advantage or asset turns the pattern requires; FY26 EBITDA fell 38%.
LOWPRICE.quote: usually manpower cost as a percentage of sales is 16-17%, at present ours is on a higher side

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is set by tender or by customer cost audit, with gross margins of 2.5–10% and metro bids won on razor-thin differentials against Chinese competitors; there is no instance across six calls of a price increase, and legacy fixed-price foreign-currency contracts forced ~INR250 crore of write-downs in FY26.
PRICING.quote: Our difference with China was hardly 0.5% in the MRS tender. That is very competitive.

BRAND.rationale: There is genuine heritage (1964, Mini Ratna, PSU-of-record status in metro and HMVs, awards and accolades cited in Jun-26) and it opens doors — sole bidder, nomination orders, DMRC export partnership — but it converts to neither premium pricing nor A&P-driven share, and 65-70% of sales are through open competition.
BRAND.quote: external awards and accolades that recognizes our leadership... leadership in engineering, leadership in innova■on

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new products appear year after year — 12x12 HMV, LAMV, 21 cu.m rope shovel, 550 HP motor grader, 35T electric dumper, Vande Bharat Sleeper, driverless metro, and now TBM and maritime cranes — with R&D and capex at all-time highs in FY26; but the innovation is import-substitution funded by low gross margins, not high margins funding R&D that then earns pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: the capex is all-■me high, the R &D expenditure is all-■me high

FORWARD.rationale: No own-store, franchise, licensing or D2C economics are discussed; the only customer-ward move mentioned is a spares warehouse model, which is too thin to judge the pattern.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: International expansion is real and compounding — exports INR62 crore (FY20) to INR830 crore (FY23) to a record $107mn order book in FY26, first-ever overseas metro rolling stock win, 73 countries, plus a Bhopal plant to lift rolling-stock capacity from ~250 to 800 cars — but no explicit domestic share figures are given, revenue guidance was missed, and mining share is admitted to be structurally eroding to lower-end and second-hand equipment.
SHAREGAIN.quote: highest ever order book. We are closing with 15,900 crores, including highest ever export order of $107 million

CULTURE.rationale: Management does disclose bad news promptly and without spin — the INR80 crore metro provision in Feb-26, the INR250 crore legacy correction and missed INR20,000 crore order-book target in Jun-26 — but the Dec-23 promises of 30-40% defence growth and sustained double-digit margins were not delivered (FY26 PAT down 50%), chairmanship has rotated repeatedly, and a 2018 contract was left uncorrected on the books for years.
CULTURE.quote: yes, we expected to reach 20,000, but we fell short by almost 4,000 crores... So we had to take the hard pill

MOATTEST.rationale: Defence has a genuine time barrier a funded newcomer cannot short-circuit — five-year tender-to-bulk-production cycles, two years of field trials, DRDO/VRDE qualification and a 40-year HMV installed base under every major missile system — but the rail/metro and mining businesses are open-tender contests against Alstom, Titagarh and Chinese bidders, and BEML itself is entering TBMs and maritime cranes from a clean sheet, which shows these adjacencies are enterable with capital.
MOATTEST.quote: in the defense sector, if a tender comes today, it will be at least 5 years by when the bulk production will start... It has to undergo extensive field trials for almost 2 years

RECURRING.rationale: There is no licence, AMC, subscription or deferred-revenue economics anywhere in the three calls; the only installed-base mechanic is tinting infrastructure placed at dealer counters (2,000+ colour bank machines per quarter, 2,500+ in Q3FY26), which pulls repeat base-paint and new-product sales — Roy explicitly links machine density to product attach ('to these counters, we add these innovative products'). Consumable pull-through, not contracted recurring revenue.
RECURRING.quote: installed more than 2,000 color bank machines. In this quarter

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is clearly intermediated — painters, contractors and builders are the route to market, and Berger raised painter incentives defensively in FY26 (a 1.5% drag on realisation) and cited contractor/builder relationships as the gating factor in metros. But the calls show this as a cost of competing rather than lock-in, with no training programmes or professional-loyalty architecture described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we increased our spends in the painter, spends which was there in reaction to the competition

TOLLROAD.rationale: Paint is a discretionary consumer purchase, not a sub-1% critical input, and the calls show the opposite of price-insensitivity: repeated industry-wide price cuts, a 4-5% price drop, and further cuts in economy emulsions to defend volume. No certification, standards or regulatory anchoring language.
TOLLROAD.quote: there was this price drop which happened to the extent of about 4.5-5%

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management explicitly refuses the low-price game — it walked away from putty volumes rather than sell at negative gross margin, and positions on premium/differentiated mix instead. No cost-culture, itemised-savings or high-asset-turn narrative appears in any of the three calls.
LOWPRICE.quote: we stayed away from from negative gross margin

PRICING.rationale: This is the clearest failure: across all three calls the company is absorbing price deflation, not taking price — a 4-5% cut lasting two years, a further 2-2.5% cut in economy emulsions persisting to Jan 2026, and value growth of 0.4% against 8.5% volume growth in Q3FY26. The lone 2.3% increase in Q2FY25 was mitigation, not pricing power; gross margin at 41.2% came from mix and raw materials, not price.
PRICING.quote: volume growth being relatively stable, but value growth being at 0.4%

BRAND.rationale: Real heritage (centenary year, new paint-can-shaped head office), sustained TV and digital A&P maintained even when margins were squeezed, and successful stretch into construction chemicals, waterproofing and wood coatings under the same name. But the brand is not converting into premium pricing or defended share — value growth is ~0% and Feb 2026 concedes marginal share loss, so the durability test is being failed on the pricing leg.
BRAND.quote: brand building has always been our priority

INNOVATION.rationale: Every call names new products with stated revenue impact — anti-dust, Easy Clean, SilkProm, Roof Cool & Seal, then DampShield, Color Plus and Silk Metallics — and Roy ties them directly to mix-led gross margin expansion, with pipeline language for the next quarter. Incomplete because R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, and the innovation is incremental formulation work rather than a fundable R&D-scale advantage.
INNOVATION.quote: these are high profit margin products, and doing quite well across the country

FORWARD.rationale: The urban initiative announced in Nov 2024 was an explicit forward-integration promise (own stores plus franchised Berger Exclusive/Experience outlets) and it was delivered — 'many new stores' by Feb 2025 and 'in excess of 1,800 stores' by Feb 2026, described as on track with positive traction. Falls short of strong because no franchise royalty stream, own-store share of sales, or D2C economics are ever quantified.
FORWARD.quote: currently the store numbers are in excess of 1,800 stores across the country

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Berger claimed share gains in Nov 2024 and Feb 2025 ('current market share is in excess of 20%') and visibly outgrew peers on volume in Q3FY25, but by Feb 2026 the market-share slide had been dropped from the deck and Roy admitted, when prompted, to a marginal loss with gains going to the new entrant. Persistent gain is therefore not evidenced across the full trajectory.
SHAREGAIN.quote: We have lost a little bit of market share... This year, there is a marginal decrease

CULTURE.rationale: Management owns bad news unprompted — admits its own prior optimism was wrong, discloses that it had pushed stock onto dealer shelves during the monsoon, concedes share loss when asked, and deliberately guides conservatively. It has hit the 15-17% EBITDA band it guided in every quarter across all three calls, stayed net cash positive throughout (Rs 918 cr by Dec 2025), kept investing in manpower, branding and stores through the downturn, and has stable long-tenured leadership under Abhijit Roy with the Dhingra family in the chair.
CULTURE.quote: we would like to be playing it safe. We don't want to say that... we will grow at double digit and then land up with 4-5%

MOATTEST.rationale: There is an articulable barrier — decades of dealer density, ~2,000 retail touchpoints and 2,000-2,500 tinting machines added per quarter, and a 100-year brand — and management notes serial MNC entrants (Jotun, Hempel, Sherwin) have never been disruptive. But the test is partly failed in real time: a well-funded copycat took ~3.5% share within a year and forced price cuts and higher painter spends, showing capital can buy a meaningful position in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: they may be again impacting the growth rate by 1-1 and a half percent, but that's about it

RECURRING.rationale: Defence spares/consumables (Rs.300-400cr/yr in Aug 2022) and MRO were repeatedly cited as an annuity tail behind capital equipment sales, and by Feb 2026 management framed MRO as a structural ROCE booster; but there is no discussion of attach rates, renewal rates, deferred revenue or customer advances funding the business.
RECURRING.quote: there will be constant MRO and support income coming from everything that you sell

TOLLROAD.rationale: Forgings are a material, negotiated share of OEM cost: the Aug 2024 and FY26 calls describe having to seek 'price repair' from European customers over years and absorbing tariff (Rs.31cr in Q3FY26, Rs.12cr in Q4) and energy cost hits rather than passing them on unnegotiated.
TOLLROAD.quote: tangible progress made on pricing support from our customers. Price repair activity which we are carrying on

LOWPRICE.rationale: The stated advantage is credibility, technology and value-added machined/differentiated parts at ~27-28% standalone EBITDA margins, not a low-price, high-turn, cost-obsessed model; cost actions (Mundhwa VRS, European cost cuts) are remedial rather than a culture-level pricing weapon.
LOWPRICE.quote: we bring in a much more credibility and much more dependability as compared to them

PRICING.rationale: Standalone margins are high and were defended through steel, freight and energy inflation (27-28% held FY25-FY26), but pricing is cost-pass-through negotiated with OEMs — years of 'price repair' in Europe and absorbed tariff costs show no ability to raise price above inflation at will.
PRICING.quote: During the quarter, company has absorbed tariff impact of about INR 12 crore.

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent new-product record — nine artillery platforms, ATAGS with DRDO, CQB carbine, naval/unmanned systems, aluminium light-weighting, aerospace jet-engine structures and landing systems — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, and the e-mobility/Tork bet was written off (Aug 2024 impairment, FY26 write-off).
INNOVATION.quote: we have nine artillery platforms, so we can compete in any category

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Repeated evidence of outgrowing end-markets — domestic CV revenue above the underlying market (Aug 2024), record PV exports into new geographies and new customers, aerospace rising from 2% to 10% of industrial exports (Aug 2022) to ~26% of Q4FY26 non-auto exports — but explicit market-share percentages versus named competitors are rarely given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: in the domestic market although the numbers have gone down in CV, production and sales, our market share has gone up

CULTURE.rationale: Long-tenured family leadership (Amit Kalyani and Subodh Tandale on all 16 calls), a conservative balance sheet through the cycle (net debt/equity 0.2 in 2022, 0.15-0.18 in FY26, first equity raise since 2010-11), ROCE explicitly targeted, and bad news disclosed promptly (Tork impairment, EV write-off, CDP liquidation); offset by promises that slipped badly — the US plant was to be profitable by FY24 and Europe 'breakeven by Q4' FY25, yet overseas losses persisted into FY26 and the German steel unit is now being wound up.
CULTURE.quote: it is not in our business practice to fund business losses in continuity, in perpetuity.

MOATTEST.rationale: Genuine time-and-qualification barriers exist in aerospace and defence — multi-year customer approvals/PPAPs, DRDO co-development, sole-source export positions — plus a five-to-seven-year track record to win offshore PV programmes; but the core forging business proved replicable enough that the European steel operation earned no returns and is being liquidated.
MOATTEST.quote: We were recently selected by an aerospace OEM as their first supplier from India for any critical components.

RECURRING.rationale: The core business is subscription/installed-base driven — 13m connected homes, 181m 5G customers, convergence cutting churn ~50% — and Indian prepaid is billed in advance, but across the 16 calls management never discusses attach rates, renewal rates or deferred revenue/customer advances as a funding source, so the classic product-upfront-plus-annuity framing is absent.
RECURRING.quote: We have seen converging Wi-Fi and mobile for our customers drops their churn by nearly 50%.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct-to-end-customer through Airtel's own retail, digital channels and distribution; the only intermediary mentioned is the local cable operator rollout model, and there is no prescriber/installer economics or trade-training language anywhere in the calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we have integrated our channels and all our channels now sell all services

LOWPRICE.rationale: 'War on Waste' is a named, durable pillar across all four years with itemised savings (site running cost down over 6% in four years despite accelerated rollouts, falling absolute diesel, 42,000 solarised sites, AI-driven cell sleep cycles), and scale is genuine — but Airtel explicitly plays the premium/quality-customer end with the industry's highest ARPU, so this is a cost culture without the low-price half of the pattern.
LOWPRICE.quote: our site running cost, which have declined by over 6% in last four years despite accelerated rollouts and addition of new technology layers

PRICING.rationale: ARPU rose from Rs.183 (Aug 2022) to Rs.211 (Aug 2024) to Rs.259 (Q3 FY26) while the company simultaneously added customers every quarter (4.4m revenue-earning adds in Q3 FY26), with an explicit premiumisation playbook — feature-to-smartphone, prepaid-to-postpaid, data monetisation, international roaming up 30% y/y; the qualifier is that step-changes depend on industry-wide tariff repair, and Q4 FY26 ARPU slipped to Rs.257 with management saying they were 'not happy'.
PRICING.quote: in the absence of tariff repair, we will continue to sweat ARPU growth leveraging feature phone to smartphone upgrades, prepaid to postpaid upgrades

BRAND.rationale: The Airtel name is repeatedly stretched into adjacencies — Airtel Black, Payments Bank, Airtel Finance/Airtel Money NBFC, Airtel Cloud, Airtel IQ, Nxtra, One Airtel — while simultaneously commanding premium pricing and taking share, which is the brand test; A&P spend itself is never disclosed on the calls.
BRAND.quote: Mobility sustained revenue market share gains to reach a lifetime high share.

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a consistent, named innovation cadence — self-optimising AI network (2022), FWA and 5G SA for uplink (2024), industry-first AI anti-spam and voice bots, AI writing ~30% of code (2026) — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified as a share of industry, and the innovation is operational/cost-led rather than a high-gross-margin R&D flywheel driving pricing.
INNOVATION.quote: Our industry first, AI powered Anti-Spam solution continues to deliver significant relief to our customers.

FORWARD.rationale: Airtel controls its own retail stores, delivery teams and digital buy/bill/pay/serve platforms and has integrated channels to sell the full converged bundle, but no store counts, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share are disclosed, so the forward-integration economics cannot be sized.
FORWARD.quote: Our sales teams and stores are tuned to selling just WiFi, irrespective of technology and we have expanded our delivery teams

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is claimed and evidenced consistently across all four years and every segment — #1 B2B player (2022), postpaid base ~45% larger than nearest competitor, DTH share gains through an industry decline, rising 5G shipment share, B2B core-connectivity share, culminating in lifetime-high mobility revenue market share in FY2026 — and it was won alongside rising ARPU and margins (India EBITDAaL margin 51%→51.7%), not bought with price.
SHAREGAIN.quote: All our businesses are delivering consistent growth and market share gains.

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in 2022 were delivered by 2026 — the 5G rollout plan, no further material spectrum spend, and deleveraging from 2.52x to 1.02x net debt/EBITDAaL with Rs.24,250 crores of high-cost spectrum dues prepaid, plus a progressive dividend from Rs.16 to Rs.24; management also owns bad news on the calls ('we were little late', 'we are not happy with the ARPU increase of Rs.3', 'this is not enough' on women in the workforce), and leadership is long-tenured with an orderly Vittal-to-Sharma succession under the same founding chairman.
CULTURE.quote: We are not happy with the ARPU increase of Rs.3

MOATTEST.rationale: Some assets are genuinely hard to rebuild — the largest mid-band spectrum pool accumulated 'through auctions, M&A and trading over the last five years', 1,43,000 km of fiber in three years, 45 million home passes, subsea cables and Nxtra's gigawatt data-centre build — but this is a licensed duopoly whose economics were themselves reset by a well-funded new entrant within a few years, and the calls give no articulated reason a comparably funded challenger could not close the gap again.
MOATTEST.quote: this well thought out strategy for spectrum acquisition through auctions, M&A and trading over the last five years

RECURRING.rationale: Telecom is inherently subscription/recharge-based with prepaid billed in advance, and management tracks the installed base and churn closely (churn cut from 2.9% to 2.4% in FY2024; convergence cuts churn ~50% per the May 2026 call), but across all nine calls there is no discussion of deferred revenue or customer advances as a funding source, nor of attach/renewal rates on a front-end product sale.
RECURRING.quote: we have seen converging Wi-Fi and mobile for our customers drops their churn by nearly 50%

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct-to-consumer through Airtel's own integrated channels, stores and digital journeys, not through independent professionals or prescribers who choose on the customer's behalf; the May 2025 and Feb 2026 calls emphasise channel integration and distribution productivity rather than trade training or expert recommendation.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: all our channels now sell all our services, which has driven our acceleration

TOLLROAD.rationale: Connectivity is described as essential infrastructure ("the digital spine of this country") at a tiny and globally lowest share of the customer's wallet, in a three-player oligopoly — but management repeatedly says the tariff structure is "broken" and that repair depends on industry/regulatory action, which is the opposite of a supplier who prices without negotiation.
TOLLROAD.quote: India mobile tariff continues to remain one of the lowest globally and needs further repair

LOWPRICE.rationale: Every call carries the "war on waste" pillar with itemised savings — Rs.2,500 Cr network cost optimised in FY2024, Rs.2,200 Cr in FY2025, site running cost down over 6% in four years despite 5G and 45,000 rural sites — combined with the world's lowest tariffs, rising EBITDAaL margins (48% to ~52%) and high volume; the cost culture is executed at scale, not announced.
LOWPRICE.quote: we identified 60,000 high cost sites, looked into cost structure of every single site and put together a plan to optimize cost of the site

PRICING.rationale: ARPU rose steadily (Rs.209 in Q4FY24 to Rs.245, Rs.259, Rs.257) with heavy premiumisation language, but the lift comes mainly from mix upgrades rather than company-set price rises, and management openly concedes it cannot price at will — "in the absence of tariff repair, we will continue to sweat ARPU growth" and, in May 2026, "we are not happy with the ARPU increase of Rs.3".
PRICING.quote: in the absence of tariff repair, we will continue to sweat ARPU growth

BRAND.rationale: The brand is explicitly credited for the IPO reception in May 2024, is paired with lifetime-high market share plus premium ARPU positioning, and is stretched repeatedly into adjacencies under the same name — Airtel Finance, Airtel Payments Bank, Airtel Cloud, Airtel IQ, Xstream, IPTV — with exclusive content tie-ups (Apple TV/Music, Starlink) reinforcing the premium promise.
BRAND.quote: This speaks well about the brand Airtel, about our execution capabilities, high standards of integrity and corporate governance

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a regular cadence of named launches with revenue impact (FWA, IPTV, Converged Data Engine, industry-first anti-spam, telco-grade sovereign Cloud, AI code generation at ~30% of all code) and digital revenue growing 39% YoY in Q3FY26, but R&D spend is never disclosed and there is no share-of-industry-R&D framing — innovation here is deployment-led rather than R&D-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: Our digital portfolio delivered robust revenue growth and grew 39% over last year

FORWARD.rationale: Airtel owns its retail footprint (small-format stores, gender-balanced stores) and pushes D2C through its own buy/bill/pay/serve digital platforms and Xstream app, and has integrated all channels to sell all services — but no own-store count, share of sales, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share is ever quantified across the nine calls.
FORWARD.quote: we now developed four platforms for our B2C business which is buy, bill, pay, and serve

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is the single most repeated claim across the trajectory — every circle gained share in FY2024 and again in FY2025, record-high DTH share, B2B share strengthened in core connectivity, and FY2026 closing with lifetime-high mobility revenue market share — and it was bought profitably, with management deliberately exiting commoditised low-margin B2B revenue while margins still expanded.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Mobility sustained revenue market share gains to reach a lifetime high share

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in earlier calls were delivered in later ones — FY2025 capex guided lower and came in lower, Rs.42,000 Cr of high-cost DoT debt prepaid, net debt/EBITDAaL falling 2.86 (FY24) to 1.5 (FY25) to 1.1 (FY26) with a rating upgrade and a dividend raised Rs.16 to Rs.24 — alongside prompt admission of shortfalls and an orderly Vittal-to-Shashwat Sharma succession.
CULTURE.quote: We are not happy with the ARPU increase of Rs.3

MOATTEST.rationale: The replication barrier is concrete and repeatedly quantified: licensed spectrum plus 1,43,000 km of fiber deployed over three years, 45 million home passes, 45,000 rural sites, subsea cable landings and Nxtra's 1 GW data-centre build funded by a $1 billion raise — a decade and tens of thousands of crores of capex a well-funded newcomer could not compress.
MOATTEST.quote: Over the last three years, we have deployed over 1,43,000 kilometers of fiber

RECURRING.rationale: Both calls flag a growing aftermarket — spares business up 25%+ in FY23 with record spares/services orders (~Rs 3,800 cr in FY23, ~Rs 3,500 cr in FY24), plus a 35-year Vande Bharat maintenance tail and remote monitoring/diagnostics for BPCL — but the recurring stream is small versus a Rs 1.31 lakh cr project book, and the funding model is the opposite of customer-funded: advances rose only Rs 1,244 cr on record orders, contract assets sat at ~Rs 27,000 cr and FY24 operating cash flow was negative Rs 3,712 cr.
RECURRING.quote: Our relentless focus on improving our order booking in high margin spares and services business resulted in BHEL booking its highest ever orders of over INR 3,800 crores in this area.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are won through competitive public tenders to utilities, NTPC, state gencos, Railways and MoD — the buyer is the payer and price is the deciding variable; there is no prescribing professional, no trade-training programme and no channel relationship investment anywhere in either call.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: these are the power plant projects which are in line and tenders are out in the market

TOLLROAD.rationale: BHEL supplies the boiler-turbine-generator island — the single largest capital line item of a power plant, not a sub-1% critical input — and customers negotiate hard, evidenced by the 12% cut BHEL had to take on the Vande Bharat bid and price-per-MW comparisons drawn by analysts between Talcher and Lara.
TOLLROAD.quote: while BTG is the bread and butter for BHEL

LOWPRICE.rationale: BHEL bids aggressively on price but has no replicable cost culture behind it: material cost hit ~72% of sales, gross margin fell for seven straight years to 29.7%, asset turns are poor (revenue flat at ~Rs 24,000 cr for two years) and FY24 PAT collapsed to Rs 260 cr — low price without the returns.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are today at almost 72% as material costs as a percentage of sales

PRICING.rationale: This is the explicit opposite — price deflation. Management accepted a 12% reduction on the landmark Vande Bharat order, called it 'challenging', and conceded on the FY24 call that gross margin had declined every year since FY18 from ~44% to 29.7%, with recovery pinned on vendor prices and execution rather than any ability to raise price.
PRICING.quote: it is a challenging order for us, after the reduction that we have had to do in this

BRAND.rationale: BHEL invokes heritage and 'market leadership' but it converts into neither premium pricing nor profit — record order inflow of Rs 78,000 cr in FY24 coincided with PAT falling from Rs 448 cr to Rs 260 cr and a seventh straight year of gross-margin decline; there is no A&P spend, distributor leverage or consistency premium in evidence.
BRAND.quote: BHEL has reasserted its market leadership position in the segment

INNOVATION.rationale: There is genuine indigenous engineering — PFBG coal gasification for high-ash Indian coal, demonstrated flexible operation at Raigarh/Sagardighi/Trombay, IGBT propulsion, indigenised naval guns and a dedicated Director (Engineering & R&D) — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, gross margins are falling not high, and commercialisation is still MoU-stage rather than revenue-generating.
INNOVATION.quote: BHEL's in-house developed PFBG technology, the only proven technology for gasification of high-ash Indian coals

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Real share gains are cited — 9.6 GW of thermal orders and record Rs 78,000 cr inflow in FY24, ~30% of FGD tenders, industry-segment inflow the highest in 13 years, and 38 naval guns won in 1.5 years versus 44 in the prior 30 — but the pattern's disqualifier applies: the share was won while gross margin fell for a seventh year and operating cash flow went to negative Rs 3,712 cr.
SHAREGAIN.quote: in 30 years we got orders for 44 guns, and in 1.5 years we've got orders for 38 guns

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in May 2023 — contract-asset liquidation and cash realisation in FY24/FY25 — were not delivered; FY24 operating cash outflow widened to Rs 3,712 cr, contract assets stayed at ~Rs 27,000 cr and PAT halved, while management repeatedly declined guidance, deferred basic disclosure 'offline', restated/reclassified financials, and leaned on provision write-backs (Rs 2,366 cr withdrawn vs Rs 1,371 cr created in FY23). Leadership is also unstable in the PSU pattern: Shinghal exited after FY24, Murthy took charge holding additional charge of Director (Finance), with no permanent CFO until FY2026.
CULTURE.quote: we are expecting in FY '24 as well as FY '25, quite a good numbers on the contract asset being realized

MOATTEST.rationale: Some barriers are concretely articulable — ~10 GW/year of BTG manufacturing capacity, effectively one domestic competitor in large thermal sets, decades of nuclear and naval-gun qualification, and the only proven high-ash coal gasification technology; but the barrier does not convert into returns, and BHEL is itself dependent on an eroding outside vendor base for balance-of-plant, which is the reverse of an un-replicable position.
MOATTEST.quote: we are having a capacity of around 10 GW every year, year on year we can do it

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Across all 14 calls demand is created by mass consumer marketing (Amitabh Bachchan, Pankaj Tripathi, KBC sponsorship, 'Bikaji Khao London Jao' consumer offer) and retail distribution reach, not by professionals or prescribers recommending the product; no trade-training or expert-channel lock-in is ever described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we roped in Mr. Pankaj Tripathi as a celebrity, and this was more towards UP and nearby markets

TOLLROAD.rationale: Bikaji sells a discretionary branded consumer snack, not a small-but-critical input into another business's cost base; the calls repeatedly show retailers destocking to wait for schemes/GST cuts, the opposite of price-insensitive toll-road behaviour.
TOLLROAD.quote: these retailers started destocking... he brought this inventory down to 5, 6, and he did not purchase in anticipation

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly cites itemised cost programmes — freight management, depot siting, long-term raw-material contracts, plants placed near core markets to cut logistics — and runs a high-volume/low-margin model, but there is no no-frills price-leadership culture; they compete on brand and campaigns, and EBITDA sits at only 12-14%.
LOWPRICE.quote: be it managing freight at the right place, opening depots at a different place or be it cost at a raw material level where we have done long term contract

PRICING.rationale: They pass on input inflation promptly and without visible volume loss (2-2.5% in Oct 2024, ~3% in April 2026, with Q4 FY26 volume growth of 16%), but this is cost pass-through rather than pricing above inflation, and they concede grammage cuts and give grammage back when commodities cool — closer to price-neutrality than true pricing power.
PRICING.quote: in spite of certain price being passed to the consumer, yet we haven't seen any slowdown in terms of the demand

BRAND.rationale: Genuine 1940s Haldiram-family heritage narrated in Call 1, sustained A&P (rising from ~0.5% to 2% of sales yearly, 3-4% in festive quarters) behind Amitabh Bachchan and category campaigns that visibly lifted Bhujia growth to 16-17%, plus stretch into sweets, papad, western snacks, frozen and bakery under the same name and a 2026 logo/packaging relaunch.
BRAND.quote: Bhujia Ho Toh Bikaji campaign, which we started in September month... has grown at upward of 16%, 17%

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches appear each year (khakra, multigrain bhujia, roasted namkeens in FY23; kaju katli and ladoo in FY25; bakery/artisanal via The Hazelnut Factory), but no R&D spend is ever disclosed, gross margins are commodity-driven at 32-35%, and innovation is line-extension rather than a funded R&D engine.
INNOVATION.quote: There are a lot of innovation which we and across the industry is doing in the sweet category

FORWARD.rationale: A real move toward the customer over the period — The Hazelnut Factory stake raised from 40% to ~48% with 23 retail stores doing INR47 crore in Q3 FY26 and 10 more planned, a Bikaji QSR, a Bikaji Bakes JV, and e-com/q-com reaching 3% of sales and doubling — but own-retail remains a small fraction of a INR2,994 crore business, with no franchise-royalty model.
FORWARD.quote: we delivered INR47 crore business from 23 stores as on date and the target is to open at least 10 stores next year

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Direct reach was grown methodically from 2.08 lakh outlets (Sep-23) to the promised 3.5 lakh (FY26) against 1.4 million total reach, with cited share of ~58-59% in Assam and 5%+ in newly entered Chhattisgarh and exports crossing INR100 crore; but explicit share numbers are sparse and management admits losing ground in Delhi, while FY26 volume growth of 9.5% suggests share gain is uneven.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Delhi is one state which has not done so well... competitive intensity is fairly high. And I think, when we look back, we also haven't done or could not do as much for Delhi

CULTURE.rationale: Family-controlled with long-tenured operators (CFO since 2015, same CFO/COO on every call) and a record of promises kept — the FY25 pledge to reach 3.5 lakh outlets by FY26 was explicitly delivered — plus candid admissions on Delhi, western snacks and quarter-4 supply loss; against this, several board exits, guidance that slipped from 'double-digit EBITDA' ambitions to 12-14% with PLI flattering the numbers, and serial small acquisitions temper the picture.
CULTURE.quote: So, we delivered the target what we have taken for ourselves was to cross 3.5 lakh outlets, which is what team has done

MOATTEST.rationale: There are hard-to-copy elements — a five-decade Bikaneri Bhujia lineage tied to moong dal grown only near Bikaner, a 5,000-women handmade papad operation in a category with only Lijjat as an organised peer, and a decade-plus of plants placed beside core states with 3.5 lakh direct outlets — but a well-funded entrant faces no time-, capital- or data-based barrier that money could not rebuild, as evidenced by intense competition in Delhi and in western snacks.
MOATTEST.quote: moong dal is only crop produced and farm near by the Bikaner... That's why Bhujia is famous from the Bikaner

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit, rising share numbers are quoted in every call and delivered across years: Glargine 3%→9%→mid-teens (FY23 guide met by FY25), Ogivri/Fulphila ~19-20% moving to 'nearly a fourth' by Q3FY26, Hulio market leader in Germany, Yesintek at ~a fifth of the ustekinumab market, Yesafili ~20% in Turkey. Share is won on tenders/formularies rather than bought with credit, and it is paired with improving biosimilar EBITDA (40% FY26 growth).
SHAREGAIN.quote: we started this year with a sub 3% market share, and we've moved that towards 9%... Ogivri and Fulphila continue to hold nearly a fourth of the market in the U.S.

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly concedes structural price deflation in both segments — generics PBT hit by 'price erosion' (Q1FY25) and biosimilars sold via formulary bidding and tenders; the best case offered is 'stable' pricing, never price increases.
PRICING.quote: Pricing will, of course, erode over time... it is gradual price decline.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Biocon's products are the payer's headline cost line, not a sub-1% critical input; the whole value proposition is being the cheaper substitute, and customers switch on formulary bids and tender wins rather than 'not switching once converted'.
TOLLROAD.quote: delivering affordable, high-quality, complex therapies at scale

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Prescribers do matter ('increased pull-through at the physician level', ophthalmologists' comfort with a biosimilar), but the defining economics are absent — the paying middleman is the PBM/payer/tender authority and price sensitivity is extreme, with Viatris losing and regaining a customer purely on contracting.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: that large U.S. payer is primarily using their private label... we are in a position right now of bidding these products

LOWPRICE.rationale: The model is genuinely low-price-plus-quality at scale — vertical integration in insulins/mAbs, CalRx/Civica affordable insulin, operating-leverage-driven margin expansion (biosimilar EBITDA +40% FY26) — but there is no itemised cost-obsession culture on the calls and returns remain thin (generics EBITDA margin 8-9%, group PBT small relative to capital).
LOWPRICE.quote: Margin improvement... reflects better product and geography mix as well as operating leverage benefits as we continue to realize the benefits of economies of scale.

BRAND.rationale: There is heritage language ('extensive heritage and expertise in insulins', a track record of high quality since 2018 on adalimumab) and named product brands stretched across geographies, but no A&P spend, no premium pricing and no consumer pull — brand supports credibility with regulators and physicians, not price.
BRAND.quote: we believe we are very well positioned with our extensive heritage and expertise in insulins

INNOVATION.rationale: R&D is disclosed and regular (₹223cr/15% of ex-Syngene revenue in Q1FY23, 7-9% thereafter) with named launches each year — Yesafili, Yesintek, Kirsty, Jobevne, Bosaya/Vevzuo, liraglutide — but this is imitative biosimilar/generic development that yields share, not the high-gross-margin, pricing-power-generating innovation loop the pattern requires.
INNOVATION.quote: R&D investments for the quarter stood at 7% of revenues, reaffirming our ongoing commitment to innovation and pipeline advancement.

FORWARD.rationale: A clear multi-year forward-integration trajectory: from Viatris-led profit share in FY23, to buying the Viatris commercial business and going self-led, to a 'direct-to-market' GLP-1 launch in the Netherlands and taking full global rights to Hulio from FKB in FY26. But it is channel/commercial integration — no own stores, franchising or D2C economics.
FORWARD.quote: We launched generic Liraglutide... in the Netherlands as our first 'direct-to-market' GLP-1 in the EU... secured full and exclusive global rights for Hulio

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in old calls were largely delivered (Semglee mid-teens share, Denosumab/Aflibercept filings then launches, integration 'concluded in under 100 days'), and bad news is disclosed promptly (FDA 483 observations, the Q3FY26 shutdown that 'moderated the pace of growth', the single Syngene client hit). Against that: the Viatris deal levered the balance sheet to >$1.5bn net debt, cured by two dilutive QIPs, and leadership has churned (Mittal→Bains→Tambe) — hardly conservative through the cycle.
CULTURE.quote: we proactively addressed acquisition-related leverage through 2 successive QIPs cumulatively raising nearly $1 billion

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — a decade of capex, global Phase III trials, multi-agency GMP/EMA/FDA/TGA/ANVISA clearance, interchangeability designations and patent settlements with Regeneron/Bayer/Amgen — which a copycat cannot rebuild quickly. But each molecule attracts many equally funded entrants (adalimumab, ustekinumab, aflibercept), so the advantage is an entry barrier to the industry, not a monopoly within it, and the calls' own admission of continuous price erosion shows it does not hold pricing.
MOATTEST.quote: These inspections... the 10 observations noted in the Form-483 were procedural in nature... EMA has renewed its GMP Certificates of Compliance

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 14 calls the discussion is cement volumes, realisations, premium mix and capex; there is no mention of AMC/service contracts, subscriptions, attach rates, renewals or customer advances funding the business.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Management repeatedly stresses the trade/dealer channel (77-80%+ of sales) and treats the distribution network and sales force as a core 'commercial asset' that carried the Reliance brand transition, but no excerpt describes mason/contractor training programmes or professional prescriber lock-in.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we don't tend to look at the valuation of the brands, as well as the valuation, what I call the commercial assets... your distribution network, logistics network, and most importantly, the people

TOLLROAD.rationale: Cement is a large, negotiated, price-visible input, and the Jul 2026 call shows Birla is a price-taker whose realisations depend on what larger competitors do — the opposite of a niche critical input bought without negotiation.
